prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: authorized, traceable hospital dispensing/returns. Producers/aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway—Order Reconciliation Snapshot; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot—Priority Refill Tote Tag; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station—Batch Release Note; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk—Return Bin; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician—Cold Chain Handoff Card; Clinical Pharmacist—Dose Exception Review Slip; Hospital Courier—Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; East Tube Dispatch Console—Tube Route Exception Ticket; Charge Nurse—Cabinet Downtime Notice; Medication Safety Officer—Diversion Review Packet. Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Morrowglass validates orders/rejects invalid updates; unresolved/canceled/duplicate/superseded orders held. Cinderwake consumes Snapshot, reconciles transactions/balances; discrepancies audited/held; pharmacy authorization mandatory. Copperfield checks packaging/lot/expiry/temperature, reverifies delays; no dose decisions. Juniper pharmacist verifies patient/order/product/dose/route/time/label; high-risk independent second check recorded; mismatches held; approvals identified/timestamped. South Ward Cabinet Controller receives release note; checks approved configuration against compartment mapping/access/classes; Ready for Dispense requires checks/self-tests. Larkspur authenticates/selects active-order medication; local authorization precedes unlocking; user/order/compartment/time logged; no bypass/substitution. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses versioned/reviewed/approved location/product/threshold/role/limit configuration; mismatches rejected; thresholds never override clinical authorization. Courier collects closed ready-recorded bins; manifests reconciled before Pneumatic Tube Network admission. West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing; East checks approved routes/reachability/interlocks/conflicts. Network reports status/progress/delivery; stale/incomplete/lost communication holds; interruptions logged; stalled/unconfirmed delivery alerts Copperfield; recovery requires refreshed status/approved route. Stonewake correlates operational records/exception tickets with telemetry, assesses device/service risk, isolates faults, uses approved diagnostics, records disposition/correction/evidence/approvals. Out of Service persists until functional checks/staff approval. Pharmacist holds medication pending repeated checks; Safety Officer reviews identity/access/patient risks. IT Operations Specialist receives Packet/logs, investigates authentication/interfaces/time-sync; uses Downtime Notice for controlled incident, checks controller/network/logs, records detection/equipment, isolates repeated requests.

New part:
S227: The Medication Order Gateway retains pending requests for review rather than treating an interrupted transaction as completed.
S228: The IT Operations Specialist checks whether any transaction was interrupted before the cabinet became unavailable.
S229: The Pharmacy Verification Station is used to confirm that pending medication orders remain valid before they are re-presented.
S230: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is held from supplying medication to a cabinet that has not passed its recovery checks.
S231: The IT Operations Specialist coordinates technical troubleshooting with the Biomedical Engineer when equipment inspection or repair is required.
S232: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews medication orders affected by the outage when clinical validation is needed.
S233: The Registered Nurse uses the established clinical process for urgent medication needs while the cabinet is unavailable.
S234: The Biomedical Engineer reports completed repairs and any equipment limitations to the IT Operations Specialist.
S235: After repair, the IT Operations Specialist verifies communications, status reporting, and cabinet transaction behavior under controlled conditions.
S236: The responsible staff confirm that no unresolved transaction could cause a duplicate or missed dispense.
S237: The cabinet remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return to Ready for Dispense.
S238: The West Tube Dispatch Console uses the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record to verify capsule identity and seal status before closing its dispatch-side handoff checks.
S239: The West Tube Dispatch Console records completion of its handoff checks only after the required dispatch data are consistent.
S240: The Pneumatic Tube Network remains under monitoring while dispatch service is being restored.
S241: The Hospital Courier confirms physical receipt through the established delivery process.
S242: The West Tube Dispatch Console retains the handoff completion status for operational review.
S243: The IT Operations Specialist monitors cabinet and tube service status for recurrence during the recovery period.
S244: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, recovery checks, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
